CHIEF COMPLAINT
Pain and redness of the right big toe.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with right big toe pain and erythema that has been intermittent for approximately two weeks, with significant worsening over the past week. Patient reports the pain became severe while attending a trade show convention, limiting his ability to ambulate. He describes the pain as primarily throbbing in character, though it can become sharp and stabbing, especially with movement or prolonged walking. Patient notes he has adapted his gait to walk on his heels to minimize toe bending. The onset was not associated with any recalled injury. Patient became more concerned when the toe became red and warm to the touch. Pain is exacerbated by light pressure, including contact with bed sheets at night. Patient has tried ibuprofen 2 tablets daily without significant relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies gastric symptoms and reports tolerating spicy foods well.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history reported.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 2 tablets daily.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works on his feet daily. He is an active individual who enjoys cycling extensively (800+ miles annually on trails) and fishing. He typically wears flip-flops and rides a stationary bike with regular shoes and pedals.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Inspection reveals erythema and warmth of the right big toe. Palpation of the first metatarsophalangeal joint reveals a bone spur on the dorsum. Range of motion testing demonstrates pain with plantarflexion (approximately 10-20 degrees), with greater discomfort at end range. Dorsiflexion produces pain but less than plantarflexion. Passive motion elicits a grinding sensation. Palpation produces pain with lateral pressure over the joint and mild discomfort with medial pressure.

RESULTS
X-ray of the right foot demonstrates a large dorsal bone spur over the first metatarsophalangeal joint with significant cartilage loss consistent with arthritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hallux rigidus (first metatarsophalangeal joint osteoarthritis). Initiated conservative management with custom shoe orthotic insert and meloxicam once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Counseled patient on potential gastrointestinal side effects including heartburn and epigastric pain; instructed to discontinue medication and contact office if such symptoms develop. Advised patient to continue regular work and activities to assess treatment efficacy. If inadequate improvement in two weeks, will consider intra-articular injection or surgical intervention including joint debridement or arthrodesis. Patient to follow up in two weeks for reassessment.
